steps: Navigate to Testing program > Policies
Click on a policy row in the list to open the policy details view.
In the left "Sections" panel, click the desired section to select it (the document scrolls to that section).
Click "Show only this section" beneath the Sections list to narrow the document to that section.

Choose the desired control from the "Select a control" dropdown.

prerequisites: A policy (compliance manual) whose document actually has parsed headings, so the left 'Sections' panel renders — a policy with no detected headings shows no Sections panel at all and the flow cannot start.

The policy must be opened at its current/active version, not an older archived version — the backend rejects section-control writes on a non-ACTIVE FirmPolicyVersion and the UI marks the panel read-only in that case.

The recording account needs the Firm Oversight feature enabled for the tenant and the FIRM_OVERSIGHT_ADMIN_ACCESS role action, since GET/POST/DELETE on section-control links all require it (views_section_controls.py) — this is the same permission the rest of the Testing program module needs, so it is presumably already satisfied for whatever account records these workflows.

workflows.title: How to export all of an entity's testing data

In the "Export testing program" dialog, set the "Start date" and "End date" fields to the desired range, or click one of the preset buttons — "YTD", "Last quarter", or "Last month" — to fill them automatically. Note this exports the whole testing program company-wide, not just the entity you launched it from.
Click "Prepare export" to queue the export job.
A "Preparing your export" confirmation toast appears. Click "Open export" in the toast to go to that export's detail page under Settings > Exports.

This matches the same pattern found separately with policy WSP ingestion and account-statement processing: staging appears to lack a registered async-worker deployment for at least some background jobs, so anything depending on one may never finish here even though the trigger/UI side is completely correct. Worth re-testing closer to actual recording time — if it's still stuck, this step may need to be recorded against production instead of staging, or flagged to Hadrius eng as a staging-infra gap.

workflows.title: How to correct how a policy's sections were parsed
workflows.purpose: Correct mis-parsed policy headings, hierarchy levels, or split sections using the update sections editor so corrections persist across future document uploads.
steps: Navigate to Testing program > Policies
Locate a policy that already has an uploaded document, and click the row's actions button (three dots icon) on the right
Click "Update sections" in the dropdown menu to open the section hierarchy editor
In the "Update sections" dialog, select the checkbox next to one or more parsed sections that need adjustment, or shift-click a second row to select everything between them
Click "Shift left" to promote the selected section(s) up a hierarchy level, or click "Shift right" to indent them under the section above
Click "Merge up" to combine the selected section(s) into the section directly above them
Alternatively, hover over an individual section row to reveal its inline shift-left, shift-right, and merge icons and use those instead
Use the "Undo" and "Redo" icon buttons in the toolbar to step back and forth through section adjustments if needed
Click "Save corrections" to persist the hierarchy rules and re-apply them to all future uploads of the policy
prerequisites: At least one policy (ComplianceManual) in ACTIVE status that already has a document uploaded (has_content = true) — the "Update sections" menu item is only shown when isCurrent && manual.has_content is true (policy_menu.tsx)
No special role/permission or feature flag is required beyond normal access to Testing program > Policies

The document's parsed sections are derived live from its headings on read (usePolicySections calls a GET .../sections/ endpoint each time, no async parsing job or approval step) — so any policy with an uploaded document has a section tree ready immediately, even if the tree is trivial (a document with no real headings still returns a valid, if flat, tree)

workflows.title: How to file a new Form U5
workflows.purpose: Initiate, complete, sign, and submit a Form U5 termination filing to FINRA for an employee leaving the firm.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > U5 filings.
Click "File New U5" to start a new Form U5 filing; this opens the multi-step filing wizard at /finra/u5/new.
On the "Preliminary information" step, use "Select employee" to choose the representative being terminated, confirm the filing firm in "Select firm", and click "Next: General information".
On the "General information" step, review personal details, verify or update fields in "Section 3: Current residential address", and click "Next: Termination information".

On the "Termination information" step, under "Section 1: Termination details" select Yes or No for "Is this a full termination?". If Yes, then under the resulting "Section 2: Date of termination" fields, choose a "Reason for termination:" and pick the "Date terminated (MM/DD/YYYY):". If No, a partial-termination section is shown instead and the Reason/Date fields do not appear. Then click "Next: Disclosures".
On the "Disclosures" step, answer the questions under each disclosure category or click "Answer \"No\" to all" for a section, then click "Next: Disclosure reporting pages".
On the "Disclosure reporting pages" step, review the disclosure reporting pages message and click "Next: Review".
On the "Review" step, review all filing information and click "Save and proceed to signatures" to create the filing record.

On the resulting "Edit Form U5 filing" page's Signatures step, under "Firm acknowledgment" enter the contact person, telephone number, and signatory name, check the acknowledgment checkbox, and click "Sign firm acknowledgment"; if an "Individual acknowledgment and consent" section is also shown, enter the printed name, check its checkbox, and click "Sign individual acknowledgment".
Click "Back to filing" to open the filing detail page for this employee's U5.
Click "Validate filing" to run FINRA validation, then once the filing is ready click "File U5 to FINRA" and confirm by clicking "Submit filing" in the "Submit U5 filing" dialog.
prerequisites: A registered employee who is ACTIVE, has a CRD number, has an initial U4 filing on record, and does not already have a U5 filing (only such employees appear in the "Select employee" picker)
That employee must have a current (non-terminated) PRIMARY firm association, so a filing firm auto-populates or can be chosen in "Select firm"

The filing firm must already have valid, real FINRA API credentials (client_id/secret) connected under Firm profile > FINRA API credentials — 'Validate filing' and 'File U5 to FINRA' call FINRA's live production filing API (api.finra.org) even for this internal sandbox company, not a safe mock, so this cannot be faked with placeholder values entered in the credentials UI

workflows.title: How to file a Form U4 amendment
workflows.purpose: Initiate and submit a Form U4 amendment filing for a representative to update registration information.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > U4 filings
Click "File New U4" to open the "Create new Form U4 filing" dialog
Select the "Amendment" option and click "Continue" to open the filing wizard
Under "Section 1: Select representative", search for the representative in "Search for a representative's name or email" and click their name from the results
Under "Section 2: Select amendment type", choose the desired amendment category (e.g. "State registration")
Click "Next: Enter amendment details" to advance to the "Enter details" step
Complete the required fields for the selected amendment type on the "Enter details" step, then click "Next: Review & submit"
Review the amendment details on the "Review & submit" step and click "Continue to signatures" to save the amendment and proceed to signatures
prerequisites: Admin role on the recording account — creating a U4 amendment is admin-gated on the backend (`@has_role_access(User.Role.ADMIN)` on the create/update endpoints), even though the 'File New U4' button itself isn't visibly restricted in the UI.

The FINRA/U4 module enabled for the tenant (`finra_api_enabled` feature flag backs `@feature_enabled(FINRA)` on the amendment endpoints and the whole People oversight > U4 filings route) — very likely already on for this tenant since it's Hadrius's internal FINRA/broker-dealer demo company and the route was confirmed to render in the prior verification pass.

At least one ACTIVE employee who is a real FINRA-registered representative: has a CRD number set AND already has an underlying FirmAssociation record (finra_profile not null). The frontend representative picker only filters on `status === 'ACTIVE' && crd_number` — it does NOT check for a firm association — but the backend create endpoint (`post_create_u4_amendment`) hard-rejects with 400 'finra/amendment/no_firm_association' if the selected employee lacks one. So an employee who merely has a CRD number typed into their profile (but was never actually synced from FINRA) will pass the picker but fail at the final 'Continue to signatures' submit.

If 'State registration' or 'SRO registration' amendment type is used (as in the plan's example), no pre-existing registration data is actually required — the form lets the operator fill values from scratch — so this is not an extra precondition.
suggestedSetupSteps: If the U4 directory is empty or no employee appears to have a prior FINRA sync (no existing U4 filings, or the chosen representative's CRD is unverified), navigate to that employee's profile page under People > Employees.
Click the employee actions menu and choose "Connect to FINRA" (or "Sync from FINRA").

Enter the representative's CRD number and date of birth, then submit — this tenant's FINRA integration is mocked (company 1013 is classified INTERNAL/sandbox, so `finra_client()` always uses `call_mock=True`), so the sync succeeds immediately without any real external FINRA connectivity and creates the underlying FirmAssociation record needed for amendments.

Confirm the sync completed (toast says "Sync successful" / "Account connected and synced"), then return to People oversight > U4 filings and use this employee as the representative in Section 1 of the amendment wizard.

workflows.title: How to file a new Form U5 for a departing representative
workflows.purpose: Create a Form U5 termination filing for a departing representative through the seven-step 'New Form U5 filing' wizard, collect the firm and individual signatures, then validate and file it to FINRA from the filing's detail page.
steps: Navigate to People oversight > U5 filings (the "Form U5 directory" page opens)

Click "File New U5" to open the "New Form U5 filing" wizard at /finra/u5/new, with a vertical stepper listing "Preliminary information", "General information", "Termination information", "Disclosures", "Disclosure reporting pages", "Review", and "Signatures"

On "Preliminary information" under "Section 1: Select representative", type into the "Search for a representative's name or email" box under "Select employee" and choose the departing representative from the results; under "Section 2: Firm information" choose the firm from "Select firm" if more than one primary firm association exists (it auto-selects if there is only one), then click "Next: General information"

On "General information", review the read-only "Section 1: Personal details" and "Section 2: Office of employment" fields, then under "Section 3: Current residential address" fill in any missing required fields ("Address line 1", "Start date", "City", "State", "Country", "Zip code") — these are pre-filled from the employee's most recent address on file if one exists — then click "Next: Termination information"
On "Termination information" under "Section 1: Termination details", answer "Is this a full termination?" using the Yes/No radio

For a full termination, select a "Reason for termination:" radio ("Deceased", "Discharged", "Other", "Permitted to resign", or "Voluntary"); if you chose Discharged, Permitted to resign, or Other, fill in the required "Termination explanation:" textarea, then pick the date in "Date terminated (MM/DD/YYYY):" using the "Select termination date" date picker
Answer "Is this a multiple termination with one or more firms affiliated with the filing firm?" under "Affiliated firm termination", then click "Next: Disclosures"

On "7. Disclosure questions", answer each Yes/No disclosure question in sections 7A–7F (or check the optional "Disclosure certification checkbox" to skip 7A, 7C, 7D, 7E if the firm already reported them on Form U4), then click "Next: Disclosure reporting pages"
On "Disclosure reporting pages" — a read-only confirmation screen that always shows "No disclosure reporting pages required" — click "Next: Review"
On "Review", check the summarized filing details, then click "Save and proceed to signatures"; a "U5 filing created" toast appears and the stepper advances to "Signatures"

Under "Firm acknowledgment", fill in "Person to contact for further information", "Telephone # of person to contact", and "Type or print name of appropriate signatory", tick the checkbox labeled "I verify the accuracy and completeness of the information contained in and with this form.", and click "Sign firm acknowledgment" (toast "Signature submitted")

Under "Individual acknowledgment and consent", confirm the pre-filled "Type or print name of individual" field, tick the checkbox labeled "Electronic signature of individual", and click "Sign individual acknowledgment" (toast "Signature submitted")
Return to People oversight > U5 filings and click "View" on the new row to open the filing detail page at /finra/u5/{id}

Click "Validate filing"; if a dialog titled "Employee SSN Required" appears, enter the SSN and click "Validate" to retry — once validation succeeds a "Filing validated" toast appears and the status badge changes to "Ready to file: Please file to FINRA"
Click "File U5 to FINRA", then in the "Submit U5 filing" dialog click "Submit filing" to send the filing to FINRA (toast "U5 filing submitted")

The representative needs at least one active primary ("PRIMARY" firm_type) firm association or the "Select firm" dropdown will show no options

workflows.title: How to complete and submit a branch exam task questionnaire

workflows.title: How to file a new branch registration (Form BR)
workflows.purpose: Start an initial Form BR to register a new branch office from Branch filings, work through the filing sections, create the draft, and sign it.
steps: Navigate to Branches > Branch filings
Click "New branch filing". The "Select branch filing type" dialog opens.

Select "Register a new branch office" and click "Continue". The "New Form BR filing" page opens (/finra/br/new) with the progress steps General information, Registration information, Other business activities, Branch office arrangements, Associated individuals and locations, Review.

In "Section 1: General information", fill "Applicant name", "Applicant CRD", choose the "Filing firm", and enter the branch address fields ("Address line 1", "Country", "State", "City", "Zip code", "Branch phone number") and answer "Is private residence?". Click "Next: Registration information".
Complete the "Registration information" step and click "Next: Other business activities".

Complete "Other business activities", "Branch office arrangements" and "Associated individuals and locations", clicking the "Next: ..." button after each (use "Previous" to go back; validation errors appear under "Please fix the following errors before continuing").
On the "Review" step, check the summary and click "Submit". A toast "BR Filing Created Successfully" appears and a "Signatures" step is added.
On the "Signatures" step, read the certification, then fill "Date (MM/DD/YYYY)", "Printed name", "Telephone number", optionally "Email address (optional)", and "Title".
Tick "Electronic signature of appropriate signatory" and click "Sign Filing".
A toast "Filing signed successfully" appears and you are taken to the filing's detail page (/finra/br/<id>), from which the filing can be validated and submitted to FINRA.

workflows.title: How to create a visibility (information barrier) policy for instant messages
workflows.purpose: Create a scoped visibility barrier policy that controls which employees' instant-message communications a defined group of people can or cannot see.
steps: Navigate to Communications > Instant messages, then open the "Instant messages" settings page ("Message management") and select the "Policies" tab
Click "New policy" to open the policy wizard on step 1, "Create visibility policy"
In the "Policy name" section, enter a name in the "Name" field (e.g., matching placeholder "e.g., Trading Desk Visibility Policy")
In the "Define policy scope" section, under "Include people who are", type into the search field and select at least one group or employee from the dropdown to add it as a scope chip
Optionally, under "Except:" in the same builder, search and select groups or employees to exclude from the scope
Optionally, click the "Preview" button to open the "Policy preview" panel and confirm which employees match the scope
Click "Next: Define visibility rules" to advance to step 2
In the "Policy status:" dropdown, leave it set to "Active" or change it to "Draft"
Under "Include communications from", type into the "Search groups, employees, or aliases to include..." field and select items to add them as chips
Optionally, under "Exclude communications from", type into the "Search groups, employees, or aliases to exclude..." field and select items to exclude
Review the plain-language summary under "Section 3: Rule summary", then click "Create policy" — a "Policy created" toast confirms success and you are redirected to the Policies tab

Company must have the "comms_review" feature enabled and the Instant Messages tab visible (instantMessagesTabVisible) for the Communications > Instant messages nav item and header actions to appear
At least one employee group or employee must exist in People > Employees/Groups to add to "Include people who are" — the wizard blocks "Next" until at least one is selected
IM aliases (if you want to include/exclude by alias rather than employee/group in step 2) must already be linked via the Alias tab — optional, not required to complete the flow

workflows.title: How to create a new approval workflow

workflows.title: How to create a new marketing project

workflows.title: How to configure document expiration and renewal rules
workflows.purpose: Turn on firm-wide expiration for approved marketing documents, set default durations and near-expiration windows, choose auto-renew or auto-resubmit behavior, add a per-document-type override, and configure who is notified when documents approach or pass expiration.
steps: Navigate to Marketing > Projects, then click "Settings" in the page header (opens /marketing/settings).
Click the "Expiration dates" tab.
In the "Firm-wide expiration" card, turn on the switch (aria-label "Firm-wide expiration"); the card's fields become editable.
Under "Default document expiration", enter a value and unit in "Default expiration".
Optionally set the "Near-expiration badge" and "Near-expiration notification" windows.
Under "When an approval expires", toggle either "Renew it automatically" or "Resubmit it for a new approval" (both off means the approval simply lapses).
If "Resubmit it for a new approval" is on, fill the "Resubmit [N] days [before/after] the expiration date." row with a day count and timing.
In the "Expiration by document type" card, click "Add document type override".

In the "Add document type override" dialog, pick a type in the "Document type" combobox and set "Expires after", then click "Add override"; a row appears in the table with "Expiration", "Auto-renew" and "Auto-resubmit" columns.
Optionally toggle the row's "Auto-renew" or "Auto-resubmit" switch.
In the "Per-document overrides" card, toggle the switch to let document owners turn auto-resubmit on or off for their own documents.
In the "Expiration notifications" card, turn on "Enable", then tick the "Admin", "Approver" and/or "Submitter" checkboxes for the "Expiration approaching" and "Document expired" rows.
Click "Save changes" in the page header; a "Settings saved." toast confirms.

workflows.title: How to archive a flagged exception

steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview
In the "Exceptions" table, click the exception row you want to archive to open its detail page.
Click the red "Archive" button in the page header (only visible to admins).

In the "Archive exception" dialog, read the warning alert (for a live, non-sandbox flag it says the flag "leaves the review queue for everyone") and type the explanation in the "Archive reason" field.
Click "Yes, archive this live flag" (the button reads "Archive exception" when the flag is sandbox output) to confirm.
Verify the "Flag archived" toast, the "This flag is archived" banner at the top of the page showing who archived it and the reason, and that the header button now reads "Unarchive".

suggestedSetupSteps: Ensure trade data exists (custodian feed or CSV/XLSX upload at /account-surveillance/import_data).

workflows.title: How to save and reuse a custom trade search

steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Trades

In the table toolbar, click "Filters" to open the "Trade filters" side panel (sections: "Saved search", "Date and time", "Executed by", "Account", "Security", "Value"; a "Representative" section also appears when reps do not share all clients).

Set your criteria — for example expand "Security" and type a ticker in "Symbol", and expand "Date and time" and click the "Last 30 days" chip. Filters apply to the table immediately; the "Filters" button shows a count of active filters.

Click "Save as new". The saved search becomes the selected search in the "Saved search" dropdown.

Some trades ingested (custodian feed or CSV/XLSX import) so the filtered table has rows to show — saving a search itself does not require trades.

Verify the "Exception escalated" toast, that "Review status" now shows "Escalated", and that the header now shows "Reopen exception" instead of "Escalate"/"Close".

Create an open exception via a rule run (Overview > "Rule library" > row menu > "Run now") or manually from Account surveillance > Trades: tick trade rows, click "Create manual exception", fill "Title", choose a severity, click "Create exception".

steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Trades
Optionally use the search box ("Search symbol, CUSIP, ISIN, order ID, or external ID...") or the "Trade filters" panel to narrow the blotter to the trades in question
Tick the row checkboxes of the trades to include; a "N trades selected" bar appears above the table and a "Create manual exception" button appears in the toolbar next to "Export"

Click "Create manual exception"; the app navigates to the "New manual exception" page (/account-surveillance/rules/violations/new) with breadcrumbs Account surveillance > Trades > New manual exception
In the "Reason for flagging" card, enter a "Title" (required); optionally fill "Description" and "Initial note"
Review the "Trade details" section listing each selected trade (symbol, side, quantity, date, account, rep)
In "Parties involved", confirm the "Subject representative" (auto-derived from the trades, or pick one with "Select representative" if the trades span more than one rep)
In the right-hand rail, choose a "Severity" (Low / Medium / High) via "Select severity" (required)
Optionally pick a reviewer under "Assigned to" via "Select reviewer" (defaults to "Unassigned")
Click "Create exception" in the page header; the button reads "Creating..." while saving, then the app navigates to the new exception's detail page (/account-surveillance/rules/violations/{id})
workflows.purpose: A compliance officer ticks trades in the Trades blotter and opens a manual exception covering them when no automated rule caught the activity.
prerequisites: Account surveillance module enabled for the company (sidebar tab not hidden by module permissions)
Ingested trade data so the Trades blotter has rows to select
Selection is scoped to the current page: changing filters, sort, or page clears ticked rows
workflows.title: How to create a manual exception from selected trades

steps: Navigate to Account surveillance > Overview
Scroll to the "Exceptions" table; optionally narrow it with the filter pills ("All", "Open", "New", "Escalated", "Closed"), "Filter by rule", or the "Search exceptions..." search

Tick the row checkboxes of the exceptions to update; a "N flags selected" bulk action bar appears above the table with "Close", "Escalate", "Reopen", "Archive", a "Set severity" select and an "Assign to" select
To change risk level, open the "Set severity" select and choose "High", "Medium", or "Low"; the update applies immediately and the selection clears
Tick the rows again if you also want to reassign them
To assign a reviewer, open the "Assign to" select and choose an admin by name (or "Unassigned"); the update applies immediately and the selection clears
Confirm the "Risk level" column now shows the new severity for the affected rows (Low / Moderate / High)
Optionally click "Clear" on the bulk action bar to drop any remaining selection
workflows.purpose: An admin selects several exceptions in the Overview table and sets their risk level or assigns them to a reviewer in one action.
prerequisites: Signed in as an admin (useIsAdmin): row checkboxes and the bulk action bar are admin-only
At least two existing exceptions (rule-generated or manual) in the Exceptions table
At least one other admin employee to appear in the "Assign to" list
Not in the "Archived" pill view, where only "Unarchive" is offered
suggestedSetupSteps: If no exceptions exist: Navigate to Account surveillance > Trades, tick a few trades, click "Create manual exception", fill Title and Severity, click "Create exception" (repeat once more)
